body:
- **Request:** Match Apple's Liquid Glass rendering/refraction as closely as the supplied iOS reference scenes allow, with exact visual parity as the owner's target. Investigate the supplied localica-reference examples and the existing [Liquid Glass field guide](https://github.com/anastaci1a/localica/tree/a9105ba/docs/liquid-glass); consolidate shared optics rather than tuning each screen separately.
- **Done when:** Matched circle, capsule and panel scenes over checkerboards, text, light/dark surfaces and artwork demonstrate reference-matched lensing, rim width/illumination, scattering, tint and readable body; foreground remains crisp.
- **Done when:** Central landmarks remain registered without unexplained directional bias while curved shoulders retain the reference's compression. Nested shapes share concentric corner-circle centers where applicable; holds, drags, morphs and reversals keep geometry coherent.
- **Done when:** Side-by-side still/frame-sequence comparisons cover API33+ shaders and API26–32 fallback, including source/window offsets. Record concrete remaining deviations and performance/legibility results; do not claim parity from pure geometry tests alone.
- **Done when:** Quantify matched demo/video frame sequences for background landmark displacement, effective blur, apparent curvature and pressed-state lensing, using unobstructed backdrop references and reporting capture/scale/compression uncertainty. Static screenshots alone must not be treated as recovery of Apple shader parameters.
- **Done when:** Interaction illumination starts at the contact point, spreads through the material and appropriate nearby glass, and releases/cancels continuously; compare actual frame sequences, not only a global brightness toggle.
- **Context:** This is a reference-based visual recreation goal, not access to Apple's proprietary rendering algorithm. [Apple's primary overview](https://developer.apple.com/videos/play/wwdc2025/219/) covers dynamics (1:29), adaptation (6:00) and principles (10:31). Supplied reference images were inspected privately and are not republished here.
- **Related work:** Coordinate #194/#217 legacy sampling, #209 shared deformed boundaries and #218 motion channels. Preserve their focused acceptance tests rather than duplicating tickets or replacing evidence with generic blur/opacity adjustments.

comments.body:
- First quantitative reference: [Apple's dunes demo at ~179s](https://developer.apple.com/videos/play/wwdc2025/219/?time=179). After background-only affine registration (mean residual ~0.66/255), nine ridge landmarks move only 0–2 full-HD pixels; five local edge fits estimate ~0.5–0.6px normal-to-ridge displacement. One edge does not identify a complete 2D displacement field.
- The same-sized Localica crown model (radius234px, depth1.35) predicts ~24.6px displayed displacement for the corresponding center-column ridge. This is production optical arithmetic against an approximate reference circle, not an Android screenshot or a universal Apple profile. It motivates independently matching interior registration and peripheral bend rather than raising one global depth parameter.
- [Apple's press example at ~731–732s](https://developer.apple.com/videos/play/wwdc2025/219/?time=731) contracts the capsule height ~8.7%; a label-free interior patch brightens ~25.6/255 RGB while an exterior patch changes ~0.14/255. The pair constrains combined visible behavior, not a recovered lighting equation or propagation duration.
- Effective blur remains confounded by texture, scaling/encoding and spatially varying lensing; no exact Apple blur radius was recovered. Next: matched native renders and denser contact-onset frames. Reference assets remain private/local; these links point to Apple's public video.

- Reference calibration should distinguish clear controls from regular/frosted material. In [Apple's actual UIKit slider demo at ~18:12](https://developer.apple.com/videos/play/wwdc2025/284/?time=1092), same-frame gray track edges under the active glass differ from uncovered edges by about +0.12/−0.06 full-HD pixels; their effective edge widths are nearly equal. Two additional active frames support the same sharp, registered core. This measures the normal-to-edge component, not the complete optical field or a universal bound.
- A separate [regular/frosted text example at ~11:51](https://developer.apple.com/videos/play/wwdc2025/219/?time=711) supports substantial blur. Reconstructing the exposed glyphs from a later frame gives a scene-specific effective Gaussian sigma around 12 displayed-HD pixels. Freezing that source blur and testing two other frames reduces patch RMS error from ~14–15/255 without blur to ~1.6/255. Alignment and intensity gain/offset are refitted per frame: this validates a conditional blur hypothesis, not a frozen complete renderer.
- Camera defocus, scale, video encoding and adaptive tone remain confounded. These values must not become universal Apple shader constants. The outer rim still lacks reliable correspondence, and occlusion/clipping prevent a defensible contact-light latency estimate.
- Suggested next check: matched native indexed-grid renders with zero-power registration first, followed by separate clear-core, peripheral distortion and regular-material blur calibration. Keep contact-origin illumination and foreground sharpness independently testable. No private reference assets have been uploaded.

Additional calibration from [Apple's UIKit slider at ~18:12](https://developer.apple.com/videos/play/wwdc2025/284/?time=1092) now distinguishes the sharp core from localized rim distortion:

- Joint top/bottom gray-track fits remain within about 0.18 displayed-HD pixels at 36–51 px inward from the rim highlight. At 11 px inward, top edges move −2.20…−2.66 px and bottom edges +3.41…+5.88 px across the training frame and two held-out active frames. Opposite shifts support local widening rather than one common registration offset.
- The final 8 px are excluded consistently because highlights make correspondence ambiguous. A symmetric boundary-localized model fitted only to the 1092s frame gives held-out edge RMS 0.566/0.821 px, versus 1.708/1.238 for identity and 1.443/1.206 for a core-wide adjustment. Added asymmetry does not improve both held-outs.
- These are observed image-feature displacements. An inverse shader must map the displaced output edge back to its original source coordinate. A single horizontal bar cannot identify tangential distortion; approximate outline, changing pose/material state and video encoding remain limitations.

[Experimental PR #240](https://github.com/anastaci1a/localica/pull/240) tests a bounded, opt-in inverse map on real AGSL and legacy-mesh adapters using coordinate-coded images. Its fixed candidate modestly improves the approximate matched-shape held-out inverse residuals (0.981/0.803 px versus 1.158/1.140 for the existing depth-1.35 model). The excluded outer band uses an explicitly uncalibrated continuation. Native adapter results are pending; shipped defaults are unchanged. This is a controlled comparison, not Apple parity or a recovered proprietary equation. Blur and illumination remain separate calibration targets; no private reference frames are published.

Two useful updates for calibration:

- [Experimental PR #240](https://github.com/anastaci1a/localica/pull/240) now passes its unchanged coordinate-grid probe on both API 26 and 36 at `95d4aee4748e2005bfc7539a5ae9c203bb6ec8ec` ([run](https://github.com/anastaci1a/localica/actions/runs/38737674015)). All six stages execute; maximum inverse-coordinate error is about 1.414 displayed pixels on the legacy path and 0.883 on AGSL. This validates the opt-in adapters against the candidate model after mesh conditioning, not Apple parity. Defaults remain unchanged.
- In [Apple's illustrated interaction sequence around 12:11.9–12:13.4](https://developer.apple.com/videos/play/wwdc2025/219/?time=731), a visually checked pair with closely matched rim outlines (about 582×323 versus 577×327 HD pixels) still changes two label-free interior patches by roughly −14/255 almost equally across RGB. Exterior registration/held-out residuals are only 1.80–2.46/255, with predicted scene motion below 0.465 pixels. This supports treating material brightness as a calibration dimension beyond outline deformation alone.

The frames are not established rest/held endpoints. Their unobserved optical/depth/tone state prevents uniquely attributing the change to illumination, blur or a particular physical model. Keep geometry, inverse displacement and photometric response separately measurable; do not infer universal press constants from this illustration. No reference frames are republished.

- New private calibration from [Apple's custom-view morph demo](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/swiftui/applying-liquid-glass-to-custom-views): the split circles expose the source background in the preceding state. Native asset is `https://developer.apple.com/tutorials/videos/com.apple.SwiftUI/liquid-glass-morph-views.mp4` (614×384; SHA256 `4feea1c34a97ae1a4853c8f38831b9c7579c739db2c1060b1f4b84d3082d3992`). Use presentation timestamps: this asset has variable frame intervals.
- A visually checked, label-free 21×21 patch at (423,60), trained at 1.133333s and checked at 1.400000/1.666667/4.066667/4.350000/4.616667s, favors modest inverse displacement plus blur. Background-only registration is effectively stationary; exterior RGB MAE is 1.10–1.13/255.
- Conditional fit: Gaussian sigma 3 decoded pixels, inverse lookup (0,+2.5)px, with nonnegative RGB gain/offset. Mean repeated-frame RMSE: 2.517, versus 2.883 for separately optimized blur-only, 2.794 for translation-only, and 3.260 for identity with fitted tone. Gain/offset are refitted per frame; these are repeated views of the same scene, not independent-scene validation.
- Approximate circle center (429,114), radius83: existing depth-1.35 crown predicts vertical lookup +9.44px; PR #240's fixed boundary profile predicts +5.52px. Their respective patch RMSEs are 3.223 and 2.755 after separately fitting blur. This source-formula comparison supports testing weaker interior/shoulder displacement; it is not an Android capture or a production change.
- Uncertainty matters: local fits within +0.15 RMSE span sigma1.5–4.5 and vertical displacement1–3.75px. Adding smooth illumination changes fitted sigma to2. Do not infer a universal depth/blur, exact 3D surface, or contact response. Identity and known-shift synthetic controls pass. Research scripts, numerical outputs and the detailed report remain in the private feedback folder; no Apple reference frames were uploaded. Next: freeze parameters on a separate scene, then compare clear-slider and regular-circle held-outs after #223 registration checks.

- Independently reconstructed the supplied Apple morph-patch analysis using NumPy/SciPy, with the official asset checksum and frame PTS verified. Held-out RMSE matches: identity 3.259794, blur-only 2.882573, translation-only 2.793594, joint sigma 3 px / inverse lookup (0, +2.5 px) 2.516500.
- Fixed source-model comparison also reproduces: crown center lookup (+1.0484, +9.4359), RMSE 3.223352; boundary defaults (+0.6135, +5.5213), RMSE 2.755390. This is source-formula arithmetic, not Android renderer parity.
- Important uncertainty: patch spans roughly 53–79% of assumed circle radius, not its center. Illumination-plane fit changes inferred blur and gives slightly different optimum under the independent method; no unique blur/depth/kernel recovery follows.
- A predeclared opposite-shoulder patch, with geometry and blur frozen before evaluating it, modestly improves RMSE from 2.946324 blur-only to 2.818052 with inward radial lookup. Mirrored left patch was rejected for insufficient source texture. Same-scene support only, not general Apple parity.
- Next validation needs additional textured positions/materials and native coordinate/adapter comparison before any global shader parameter change. No production optics change made.

- Codex owns Ana's documentation reconciliation, Apple evidence review and standalone refracting lab work on `maintenance/docs-glass-lab-222`, based on dev62 `67d700a291a632f94846901afeefe626c5fdc048`.
- Audit current contracts against code, release/PR state and owner decisions; preserve unresolved requirements explicitly. Then consolidate reproducible optical evidence and implement/test a small WebGL lab with actual source displacement and an honest fallback.
- No app renderer/shared-physics edits, candidate changes, main merge, release or signing. #406/#407 remain dot-owned; #405/PR408 remains separate.
— Codex

- Completed the assigned docs → research → real-refraction lab sequence. Docs-only PR #410 merged to main `9133e01f19c8571d1bf611e1f79770f0606c314a` after Ana explicitly authorized main integration and skipping Android checks for this scope. No app/build/workflow/version/signing changes; no release/tag.
- Live lab: https://anastaci1a.github.io/localica/liquid-glass/lab.html ; findings: https://anastaci1a.github.io/localica/liquid-glass/optics.html . Pages branch `gh-pages` at `7631266cb7955db4b0a53d53546dce84b2412fa2`; live manifest matches merged source and actual script checksum. Navigation/WebGL/expansion verified on the deployed site.
- #409 audit corrected obsolete rest/ownership/overflow rules, clarified branch-versus-release status, consolidated collaboration instructions and retained unresolved/deferred requirements. Original PR330 text is superseded by main's agents/collaboration.md; no old ancestry merged.
- #222 research: reproducible official-asset patch comparison plus a stricter frozen-photometry check. Held-out joint blur/displacement RMSE 2.609 versus identity 3.334 with training tone frozen. Same-scene evidence only; no recovered Apple height field/shader or universal preset.
- Lab: one real background texture, analytic silhouette/inverse lookup, boundary-focused and physical-cap comparison, independent blur/tone/reflection, pressure/rebound, idle sleep, reduced motion and disclosed 2D fallback. Original screenshots/GIF are public; Apple reference pixels remain private.
- Verification: 11 browser check groups passed (Chromium156/SwiftShader), 95 generated local links/assets/anchors passed, reference identity/known-shift controls passed, desktop/phone/clear/physical/scattering captures inspected. No physical-phone performance claim. Private logs: localica-feedback/docs-glass-lab; reproducible runners are in docs/liquid-glass/experiments.
- Preserved dev62 `67d700a291a632f94846901afeefe626c5fdc048` and #405 `bd7b96bacbae17523ed4b0779145b4b9975bbb05`. PR408's API26 failure is `PinchReleaseHandoffTest.longHeldCancelledPinchRestoresOriginalAnchor`; posted separately, API36 still running at last check. Dot retains #406/#407 and UI ownership.
- Next recommendation: freeze optical parameters against independent reference scenes, then compare native coordinate adapters before touching production defaults. #222 remains open; this bounded research/demo assignment is complete. No polling/new task underway.

- Taking the lab optics/preset follow-up on docs/glass-presets-222 from main e722bba. Review supports stronger peripheral displacement than the current conservative field/range; quiet interior measurements must not be generalized to the outer rim.
- Add independent edge/core controls, evidence-linked Clear/Regular/menu approximations, categorized accessible sidebar tabs, and GPU/software coverage. Review broader real-UI footage; distinguish observations from fitted constants. Refresh captures and deploy docs only; native renderer and dot-owned work untouched.
